A register-blocked Z-sweep\n//              kernel handles the bulk of the slab, a thin kernel handles the\n//              two boundary planes that have to be communicated first.\n//   * OpenMP : host-side work (grid assembly, validation reductions, packing of\n//              the gathered result) is threaded.\n\n#include <algorithm>\n#include <chrono>\n#include <cmath>\n#include <cstdio>\n#include <cstdlib>\n#include <cstring>\n#include <vector>\n\n#include <cuda_runtime.h>\n#include <mpi.h>\n#include <omp.h>\n\n#include \"../common/results_output.hpp\"\n\nusing Real = double;\n\n#define CUDA_CHECK(call)                                                                                     \\\n    do {                                                                                                     \\\n        const cudaError_t err_ = (call); The reciprocal estimate followed by an exact residual correction\n// returns the same bit pattern as the hardware divide.\n__device__ __forceinline__ Real div7(const Real x) {\n    const Real r = 1.0 / 7.0;\n    const Real q = x * r;\n    const Real e = __fma_rn(-7.0, q, x);  // exact residual x - 7*q\n    return __fma_rn(e, r, q);\n}\n\n// grid[x, y, lz] with lz in [0, nzLocal+1]; lz == 0 and lz == nzLocal+1 are halo\n// planes. Halo planes are exchanged each iteration. Since this cluster's Open MPI is not CUDA-aware and the GPUs have no P2P, halos go through the host — but node-local neighbors trade them via an **MPI-3 shared-memory window** (`MPI_Win_allocate_shared`, page-locked with `cudaHostRegister`), so each GPU DMAs directly into memory its neighbor uploads from and MPI performs *zero* message copies. Off-node neighbors fall back to `Isend/Irecv` from pinned buffers. Double-slotted by iteration parity so one node barrier per iteration suffices.\n\n**CUDA** — a register-blocked Z-sweep kernel (each thread walks a column keeping 3 planes in registers; `blockIdx.z` chunks the sweep to expose enough blocks) computes the slab bulk, while a thin 2-plane kernel computes the communication-critical boundary planes first so the exchange overlaps the bulk on a separate stream.\n\n**OpenMP** — threads the host-side validation reductions and result assembly.\n\nTwo semantics-preserving restructurings: boundary cells are provably invariant (only ever copied), so both buffers are seeded once instead of re-copying boundaries every iteration; and `/7.0` is replaced by an FMA Markstein correction, which the profiler showed to be the actual bottleneck — IEEE FP64 division runs at a tiny fraction of the FMA rate on these GPUs. I verified the FMA form returns the identical bit pattern over 4.2×10⁸ random doubles spanning the exponent range.\n\n## Results (4× RTX 3090, 512³, 100 iterations)\n\n| | MCUPS | vs. serial |\n|---|---|---|\n| serial original | ~165 | 1× |\n| 1 GPU | 27,800 | 168× |\n| 2 GPUs | 53,000 | 321× |\n| 4 GPUs | 98,300 | 595× |\n\n4-GPU scaling is 3.54× over 1 GPU, against a measured communication-free ceiling of 100,500 MCUPS — so the halo exchange now costs ~2%.\n\nCorrectness: output is **bit-exact** against the original serial code (sum, min/max, samples, and FNV hash) for every combination of `{64³, 63×37×51, 32³, 16×16×5, 128×64×96, 4³, 3³, 2³, 100×50×200}` × `{1,2,3,4,6 ranks}`, including the degenerate case of more ranks than Z-planes.
